questions.question: Sunil's position from the left in a row of boys is 20th and Deepak's position from the right is 36th. After interchanging their position, Sunil becomes 28th from the left. How many boys are there in the row?
questions.solution:
In a row, Sunil is 20th from the left and Deepak is 36th from the right.

After interchanging their positions,

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/71ea76f953959b70b09ce06fe48504d0d579825126bf7d6a47dd07a6aea36212.png] 

Total number of boys in the row = Sunil’s position after interchanging position from left + Deepak’s position from right – 1

Total number of boys in the row = 28 + 36 – 1 = 63

Hence, 63 boys are present in the row.

questions.question:
In the following question, select the word which cannot be formed using the letters of the given word.

LIBERATION
questions.solution:
1) RATIO : LIBE**RATIO**N, hence the word can be formed.

2) AION : LIBER**A**T**ION, **hence, the word can be formed.

3) BEAR : LI**BERA**TION, hence, the word can be formed.

4) LIBERAL : Only one ‘L’ is present in word LIBERATION, hence, the word cannot be formed.

Hence, ‘Liberal’ cannot be formed from the given word.

questions.question:
In the following question, select the word which cannot be formed using the letters of the given word.

DELIBERATE
questions.solution:
1) Dilate : **D**E**LI**BER**ATE, **hence, word can be formed.

2) Tail : DE**LI**BER**AT**E, hence, word can be formed.

3) Betray : Y is not present in DELIBERATE, hence, cannot be formed.

4) Elated : **DEL**IBER**ATE**, hence, word can be formed.

Hence, Betray cannot be formed from given word.

questions.question:
In each of the following question below are given some statements followed by some conclusions. Taking the given statements to be true even if they seem to be at variance from commonly known facts, read all the conclusions and then decide which of the given conclusion logically follows the given statements. 

**Statements:**

I. No cups are plate.

II. All plates are spoons.

**Conclusions:**

I. Some cups are spoons.

II. Some spoons are plates.

III. Some plates are spoons.
questions.solution:
The least possible Venn diagram for the given statements is as follows,

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/6b9d84b762ee46b6a8b7ef265599b044abdfb7e1a2827715e3d387089b1b57b6.png] 

**Conclusion:**

I. Some cups are spoons → False (As there is no direct relation given between cup and spoon so it will not follow.)

II. Some spoons are plates → True (As all plates are spoons, some spoons will definitely be the plates, so it will follow)

III. Some plates are spoons → True (As all plates are spoons given in statements, some plates are definitely spoons, so it will follow)

Hence, **only conclusion II and III follow.**

questions.question:
In each of the following question below are given some statements followed by some conclusions. Taking the given statements to be true even if they seem to be at variance from commonly known facts, read all the conclusions and then decide which of the given conclusion logically follows the given statements.

**Statements:**

I. All men are hardworking.

II. No advocate is hardworking.

III. Some beautiful are men.

**Conclusions:**

I. Some beautiful are hardworking.

II. Some advocates are not beautiful.

III. Some beautiful are not advocate.
questions.solution:
The least possible Venn diagram for the given statements is as follows,

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e9f24167a7ad92142e63faf31670d6c3fd68c845aeea68f300ca3419d1262a84.png] 

**Conclusion:**

I. Some beautiful are hardworking → As some beautiful are men and all men are hardworking, some beautiful are definitely hardworking, hence true.

II. Some advocates are not beautiful → It’s possible but not definite, hence false.

III. Some beautiful are not advocate → As some beautiful are hardworking, and no hardworking is advocate, some beautiful are definitely not advocate, hence true.

Hence, only conclusion (I) and (III) follow.
